questions.e: The probability is 4/10 × 3/9 = 12/90 = 2/15. The value 4/25 = (4/10)² assumes the first ball is put back.

questions.s: A jar contains 5 red and 3 green sweets. Ayesha takes two sweets at random without replacement. What is the probability that the two sweets are of different colours?
questions.e: Red then green is 5/8 × 3/7 = 15/56, and green then red is also 15/56, so the total is 30/56 = 15/28. Stopping at 15/56 forgets the second order, and 13/28 is the probability of the same colour.

questions.s: A quality check finds 6 faulty bulbs in a random sample of 80 bulbs from a factory. Based on this sample, about how many faulty bulbs would be expected in a batch of 2,000 bulbs?
questions.e: The sample rate is 6/80 = 3/40, and 3/40 × 2,000 = 150. The value 160 comes from rounding the rate up to 8 %, which the sample does not support.

questions.s: The table shows the items sold by a Lahore bakery in one week. What percent of the items sold were cakes?
questions.e: The total sold is 420 + 180 + 150 + 250 = 1,000, and 150 out of 1,000 is 15 %. The value 25 % is the share of biscuits.

questions.s: The table shows the number of visitors to a Hunza guest house in three months. By what percent did the number of visitors increase from April to June?
questions.e: The increase is 360 − 240 = 120, and 120 ÷ 240 = 0.5, an increase of 50 %. Dividing 120 by the June figure, 360, gives a smaller and wrong percentage.

questions.s: The probability of rain in a town is 0.3 on Monday and 0.4 on Tuesday, and the two days are independent. What is the probability that it rains on neither day?
questions.e: No rain on Monday has probability 0.7 and on Tuesday 0.6, so neither day is 0.7 × 0.6 = 0.42. The value 0.12 is the probability of rain on both days, and 0.58 is rain on at least one day.

questions.s: A spinner has 8 equal sectors numbered 1 to 8. It is spun once. What is the probability that it lands on a prime number?
questions.e: The primes from 1 to 8 are 2, 3, 5 and 7, so the probability is 4/8 = 1/2. The value 3/8 leaves out 2, which is prime, and 5/8 wrongly counts 1.

questions.s: The table shows where the 200 employees of a software firm work, by department. What percent of the Tech employees work remotely?
questions.e: There are 110 Tech employees and 66 of them work remotely: 66 ÷ 110 = 0.6, or 60 %. The value 33 % divides 66 by all 200 employees instead of the Tech group.

questions.s: Five different books are to be arranged in a row on a shelf. Two particular books must be placed next to each other. How many arrangements are possible?
questions.e: Treat the two books as one block: 4 units can be arranged in 4! = 24 ways, and the two books inside the block in 2 ways, giving 48. The value 24 forgets that the pair can swap places.

questions.s: How many different arrangements can be made using all the letters of the word KARACHI?
questions.e: Seven letters can be arranged in 7! = 5,040 ways, but the two As are identical, so divide by 2: 2,520. The value 5,040 counts swapping the two As as a new arrangement.

questions.s: A team of 3 people is chosen at random from 4 men and 3 women. What is the probability that the team contains exactly 2 women?
questions.e: There are C(7,3) = 35 teams; choosing 2 of the 3 women and 1 of the 4 men gives 3 × 4 = 12 teams, so the probability is 12/35. The value 18/35 is the probability of exactly 1 woman.

questions.s: The table shows the rainfall in Islamabad over five months. In which month was the rainfall closest to the mean monthly rainfall for these five months?
questions.e: The mean is (55 + 90 + 110 + 65 + 40) ÷ 5 = 360 ÷ 5 = 72 mm, and April's 65 mm is only 7 mm away. January is 17 mm away, so it is not the closest.

questions.s: The mean of six numbers is 14. When one of the numbers is removed, the mean of the remaining five numbers is 12. What number was removed?
questions.e: The six numbers total 6 × 14 = 84 and the five remaining total 5 × 12 = 60, so the removed number is 84 − 60 = 24. The value 2 is just the drop in the mean.

questions.s: Class A has 20 students with a mean exam score of 60. Class B has 30 students with a mean exam score of 70. What is the mean score of all 50 students?
questions.e: The total is 20 × 60 + 30 × 70 = 1,200 + 2,100 = 3,300, and 3,300 ÷ 50 = 66. Taking 65, the simple average of 60 and 70, ignores that Class B is larger.

questions.s: In a factory, machine X makes 60% of the items and machine Y makes the rest. 5% of X's items and 10% of Y's items are faulty. An item chosen at random is faulty. What is the probability that it was made by machine Y?
questions.e: Faulty from X is 0.6 × 0.05 = 0.03 and faulty from Y is 0.4 × 0.1 = 0.04, so the probability is 0.04 ÷ 0.07 = 4/7. The value 2/5 is just Y's share of all items, ignoring that the item is known to be faulty.

questions.s: A data set is 4, 8, 8, 10 and 15. If the value 15 is replaced by 30, which statement is true?
o: The mean and the median both rise by 3.
The mean stays the same; the median rises by 3.
The mean rises by 3; the median stays the same.
The mean rises by 15; the median stays the same.
questions.e: The total rises by 15, so the mean rises by 15 ÷ 5 = 3 (from 9 to 12), while the middle value is still 8. The mean does not rise by 15, because the increase is shared over five values.

questions.s: The table shows the ages of the 100 members of a cricket club. One member is chosen at random. What is the probability that the member is under 20?
questions.e: Under 20 means the first two groups: 18 + 24 = 42 members, and 42/100 = 21/50. The value 9/50 counts only the under-15 group.

questions.s: Twenty cards are numbered 1 to 20. One card is drawn at random. What is the probability that its number is a multiple of 3 or a multiple of 5?
questions.e: There are 6 multiples of 3 and 4 multiples of 5, but 15 is in both lists, so 6 + 4 − 1 = 9 cards qualify: 9/20. The value 1/2 counts 15 twice.

questions.s: The table shows whether 250 students own a smartphone, by level of study. One student is chosen at random from all 250. What is the probability that the student is at Inter level and does not own a smartphone?
questions.e: Exactly 20 of the 250 students are at Inter level without a smartphone, so the probability is 20/250 = 2/25. The value 2/13 divides by the 130 Inter students, but the student is chosen from all 250.

questions.s: In a game, a player rolls a fair die once. The player wins Rs 60 for a 6, Rs 12 for a 4 or a 5, and nothing otherwise. What is the expected amount won per game?
questions.e: The expected value is 60 × 1/6 + 12 × 2/6 = 10 + 4 = Rs 14. Counting the Rs 12 prize for only one face gives Rs 12, but it is paid for both 4 and 5.

questions.s: In a hockey league of 8 teams, every team plays every other team exactly twice. How many matches are played in total?
questions.e: The number of pairs of teams is (8 × 7) ÷ 2 = 28, and each pair plays twice, giving 56 matches. The value 28 forgets the second match between each pair.

questions.s: A café offers 4 starters, 5 main dishes and 3 desserts. A set meal is one main dish together with either one starter or one dessert, but not both. How many different set meals are possible?
questions.e: The second item can be chosen in 4 + 3 = 7 ways, so there are 5 × 7 = 35 meals. The value 60 = 4 × 5 × 3 counts meals with a starter and a dessert.

questions.s: A coin is tossed 50 times and lands heads 28 times. Based on these results, what is the experimental probability of tails?
questions.e: Tails occurred 50 − 28 = 22 times, and 22/50 = 11/25. The value 1/2 is the theoretical probability, not the experimental one.

questions.s: The table shows the favourite sport of 40 students. The data are to be shown in a pie chart. What angle should the Hockey sector have?
questions.e: Hockey is 7 out of 40, so its angle is 7/40 × 360° = 63°. The angle 90° belongs to Football, which has 10 students.

questions.s: A point is chosen at random inside a square of side 6 cm. A circle is drawn inside the square, touching all four sides. What is the probability that the point lies inside the circle?
questions.e: The circle has radius 3, so its area is 9π, and the square's area is 36: the probability is 9π/36 = π/4. Using the diameter 6 as the radius gives 36π/36 = π, which is impossible for a probability, and π/6 divides the circumference by the area.

questions.s: Ali hits a target with probability 0.6 and Sara hits it with probability 0.5. Each shoots once, independently. What is the probability that at least one of them hits the target?
questions.e: Both miss with probability 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.2, so at least one hits with probability 1 − 0.2 = 0.8. The value 0.5 is the probability that exactly one hits.

questions.s: The table shows the results of a trial on 300 tomato plants, some treated with a new fertiliser. Based on the table, the proportion of untreated plants that wilted is how many times the proportion of treated plants that wilted?
questions.e: Untreated: 18/100 = 0.18 wilted; treated: 12/200 = 0.06 wilted; and 0.18 ÷ 0.06 = 3. The value 1.5 = 18 ÷ 12 compares counts and ignores that the groups differ in size.

questions.s: The table shows the shoe sizes sold by a shop on one day. What is the mode of the shoe sizes sold?
questions.e: Size 8 was sold most often (25 pairs), so the mode is 8. The value 25 is the frequency of the mode, not the size itself.

questions.s: The letters of the word PAKISTAN are written on 8 identical tiles, one letter per tile. One tile is picked at random. What is the probability that it shows the letter A?
questions.e: Two of the 8 tiles show A, so the probability is 2/8 = 1/4. The value 1/8 forgets that A appears twice, and 3/8 counts all the vowels.

questions.s: A basket holds 4 yellow, 5 purple and 3 orange balloons. One balloon is taken at random. What is the probability that it is not purple?
questions.e: There are 12 balloons and 4 + 3 = 7 are not purple, so the probability is 7/12. The value 5/12 is the probability that it is purple.

questions.s: A fair six-sided die is rolled once. What is the probability that the result is an even number or a 5?
questions.e: The outcomes 2, 4, 6 and 5 qualify, which is 4 out of 6, or 2/3. The value 1/2 counts only the even numbers.

questions.s: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled. What is the probability that the product of the two numbers is 6?
questions.e: The pairs (1,6), (6,1), (2,3) and (3,2) give a product of 6, so the probability is 4/36 = 1/9. The value 1/18 misses the pairs that use 1 and 6.

questions.s: The table shows 100 books donated to a school library. One hardback book is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is fiction?
questions.e: Of the 45 hardbacks, 18 are fiction, so the probability is 18/45 = 2/5. The value 3/10 divides by the 60 fiction books instead of the 45 hardbacks.

questions.s: A cricket squad has 9 players. In how many ways can a captain and a vice-captain be chosen from the squad?
questions.e: There are 9 choices for captain and then 8 for vice-captain: 9 × 8 = 72. The value 36 divides by 2, but the two roles are different, so order matters.

questions.s: A student must choose 3 elective courses from a list of 7. In how many ways can she make her choice?
questions.e: Order does not matter, so the count is (7 × 6 × 5) ÷ (3 × 2 × 1) = 35. The value 210 counts ordered choices.

questions.s: Hina's scores on five tests were 72, 85, 90, 64 and 79. What is her mean score?
questions.e: The total is 72 + 85 + 90 + 64 + 79 = 390, and 390 ÷ 5 = 78. The value 79 is the median.

questions.s: What is the median of the data set 3, 9, 4, 12, 7, 10, 6, 5?
questions.e: In order the values are 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12; the middle two are 6 and 7, so the median is 6.5. The value 7 is the mean, and 9.5 comes from taking the middle two values (12 and 7) without sorting first.

questions.s: A drawer holds 3 working and 2 dead batteries. Two batteries are taken at random without replacement. What is the probability that both work?
questions.e: The probability is 3/5 × 2/4 = 6/20 = 3/10. The value 9/25 = (3/5)² assumes the first battery is replaced.

questions.s: A crate holds 6 ripe and 4 unripe mangoes. Three mangoes are picked at random without replacement. What is the probability that at least one of them is unripe?
questions.e: All three ripe has probability 6/10 × 5/9 × 4/8 = 1/6, so at least one unripe is 1 − 1/6 = 5/6. The value 98/125 = 1 − (3/5)³ treats the picks as if each mango were put back.

questions.s: The table shows the grades of 400 candidates in an examination. What percent of the candidates received a grade of B or better?
questions.e: Grades A and B together are 48 + 120 = 168 candidates, and 168 ÷ 400 = 42 %. The value 30 % counts grade B only.

questions.s: The table shows how 150 commuters in Lahore travel to work, by length of journey. One rickshaw user is chosen at random. What is the probability that this person travels more than 10 km?
questions.e: Of the 65 rickshaw users, 20 travel more than 10 km, so the probability is 20/65 = 4/13. The value 4/15 divides by the 75 long-distance commuters instead.

questions.s: The probability that a certain bus is late on any school day is 0.15. On how many of 40 school days would the bus be expected to be on time?
questions.e: The probability of being on time is 1 − 0.15 = 0.85, and 0.85 × 40 = 34 days. The value 6 is the expected number of late days.

questions.s: Events A and B are independent, with P(A) = 1/3 and P(B) = 1/4. What is the probability that exactly one of the two events occurs?
questions.e: A only: 1/3 × 3/4 = 3/12; B only: 2/3 × 1/4 = 2/12; together 5/12. The value 7/12 is the probability of at least one, which also includes both occurring.

questions.s: How many different arrangements can be made using all the letters of the word BANANA?
questions.e: The six letters include three As and two Ns, so the count is 6! ÷ (3! × 2!) = 720 ÷ 12 = 60. The value 120 divides only by 3! and forgets the repeated N.

questions.s: Bag 1 holds 3 red and 2 blue counters; Bag 2 holds 1 red and 4 blue counters. A fair coin is tossed to choose a bag, and one counter is drawn from it. The counter is red. What is the probability that it came from Bag 1?
questions.e: Red from Bag 1 is ½ × 3/5 = 3/10 and red from Bag 2 is ½ × 1/5 = 1/10, so the probability is (3/10) ÷ (4/10) = 3/4. The value 3/5 is the chance of red given Bag 1, which is the reverse condition.

questions.s: The mean height of 15 boys in a class is 160 cm and the mean height of the 10 girls is 150 cm. What is the mean height of the whole class?
questions.e: The total is 15 × 160 + 10 × 150 = 2,400 + 1,500 = 3,900 cm, and 3,900 ÷ 25 = 156 cm. The value 155 cm averages the two means without weighting by group size.

questions.s: The table shows the highest temperature in Murree on five days. What is the range of these temperatures?
questions.e: The range is the highest minus the lowest: 17 − 12 = 5 °C. The value 15 °C is roughly the average, not the spread.

questions.s: The table shows the favourite subject of the students in two sections of Grade 10. Of the students who chose Biology, what fraction are in Section B?
questions.e: Biology was chosen by 10 + 15 = 25 students, and 15 of them are in Section B: 15/25 = 3/5. The value 1/2 divides by the 30 students of Section B instead.

questions.s: The probability that a seed of a certain type germinates is 0.85. If 240 seeds are planted, how many are expected not to germinate?
questions.e: The probability of not germinating is 0.15, and 0.15 × 240 = 36. The value 204 is the expected number that do germinate.

questions.s: How many three-digit numbers (from 100 to 999) have three different digits?
questions.e: The first digit cannot be 0, so it has 9 choices; the second then has 9 (0 is now allowed) and the third 8: 9 × 9 × 8 = 648. The value 720 = 10 × 9 × 8 allows a leading zero.

questions.s: In a survey of 60 shoppers, 27 paid by card and the rest paid in cash. What fraction of the shoppers paid in cash?
questions.e: Cash payers are 60 − 27 = 33, and 33/60 = 11/20. The value 9/20 = 27/60 is the fraction that paid by card.

questions.s: The mean age of the 10 members of a hockey team is 24 years. When the coach is included, the mean age of the 11 people is 26 years. How old is the coach?
questions.e: The 11 people total 11 × 26 = 286 years and the players total 10 × 24 = 240, so the coach is 286 − 240 = 46. Giving 26 assumes the coach's age equals the new mean.

questions.s: A dart lands at a random point on a circular board of radius 10 cm. A bull's-eye circle of radius 4 cm has the same centre. What is the probability that the dart lands inside the bull's-eye?
questions.e: The probability is the ratio of areas: 16π ÷ 100π = 4/25. The value 2/5 compares the radii, not the areas.

questions.s: Two students are chosen at random from a group of 5 boys and 4 girls. What is the probability that both students are of the same gender?
questions.e: Same gender: C(5,2) + C(4,2) = 10 + 6 = 16 of the C(9,2) = 36 pairs, so 16/36 = 4/9. The value 41/81 = 25/81 + 16/81 allows the same student to be chosen twice.

questions.s: A rectangle has a length of 12 cm and a width of 7.5 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: Area is length × width = 12 × 7.5 = 90 cm². The value 39 is the perimeter, 2(12 + 7.5), not the area.

questions.s: A triangle has a base of 14 cm and a perpendicular height of 9 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: Area is ½ × base × height = ½ × 14 × 9 = 63 cm². The value 126 cm² forgets the factor ½.

questions.s: A circle has a radius of 7 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: Area is πr² = π × 7² = 49π cm². The value 14π is the circumference, 2πr.

questions.s: A trapezium has parallel sides of 10 cm and 16 cm, and the perpendicular distance between them is 7 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: Area is ½(a + b)h = ½ × (10 + 16) × 7 = 13 × 7 = 91 cm². The value 182 cm² forgets to halve the sum of the parallel sides.

questions.s: A rectangular garden has a perimeter of 46 m and a length of 15 m. What is its area?
questions.e: The length plus width is 46 ÷ 2 = 23 m, so the width is 8 m and the area is 15 × 8 = 120 m². The value 465 m² uses 46 − 15 = 31 as the width, forgetting that the perimeter counts each side twice.

questions.s: The diagonal of a square is 10 cm long. What is the area of the square?
questions.e: If the side is s, then s² + s² = 10², so s² = 50 and the area is 50 cm². The value 100 cm² treats the diagonal as if it were a side.

questions.s: A cylinder has a base radius of 3 cm and a height of 10 cm. What is its volume?
questions.e: Volume is πr²h = π × 9 × 10 = 90π cm³. The value 60π is the curved surface area 2πrh, and 78π is the total surface area.

questions.s: A cone has a base radius of 6 cm and a perpendicular height of 8 cm. What is its volume?
questions.e: Volume is ⅓πr²h = ⅓ × π × 36 × 8 = 96π cm³. The value 288π cm³ forgets the factor ⅓, and 60π is the curved surface area (slant height 10).

questions.s: A sphere has a radius of 6 cm. What is its volume?
questions.e: Volume is (4/3)πr³ = (4/3) × π × 216 = 288π cm³. The value 144π is the surface area 4πr², and 216π forgets the factor 4/3.

questions.s: Two cylinders are similar. The smaller has a height of 4 cm and a volume of 64 cm³. The larger has a height of 6 cm. What is the volume of the larger cylinder?
questions.e: The length scale factor is 6/4 = 3/2, so volumes scale by (3/2)³ = 27/8: 64 × 27/8 = 216 cm³. The value 96 cm³ scales by 3/2 only, and 144 cm³ uses the area factor 9/4.

questions.s: A cube has a total surface area of 150 cm². What is its volume?
questions.e: Each of the 6 faces has area 150 ÷ 6 = 25 cm², so an edge is 5 cm and the volume is 5³ = 125 cm³. The value 25 is the area of one face, not a volume.

questions.s: A closed box is a cuboid measuring 3 cm by 4 cm by 12 cm. What is the length of the longest straight rod that fits inside the box?
questions.e: The longest rod lies along the space diagonal: √(3² + 4² + 12²) = √169 = 13 cm. The value 12 cm is just the longest edge, and 19 cm adds the edges.

questions.s: A circle is drawn inside a square of side 8 cm so that it touches all four sides. What is the area of the region inside the square but outside the circle?
questions.e: The circle's radius is half the side, 4 cm, so its area is 16π and the region is 64 − 16π cm². The value 64 − 8π subtracts the circumference 8π instead of the area.

questions.s: A shape is a semicircle with a diameter of 14 cm. What is the perimeter of the shape, including the straight edge?
questions.e: The curved edge is half of π × 14, which is 7π cm, and the straight edge is the diameter, 14 cm: total 7π + 14 cm. The value 7π alone leaves out the diameter.

questions.s: A parallelogram has a base of 12 cm, slanting sides of 6 cm, and a perpendicular height of 5 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: Area is base × perpendicular height = 12 × 5 = 60 cm². The value 72 cm² wrongly multiplies the base by the slanting side.

questions.s: The diagonals of a rhombus are 10 cm and 24 cm long. What is the perimeter of the rhombus?
questions.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, so each side is √(5² + 12²) = 13 cm and the perimeter is 4 × 13 = 52 cm. The value 120 is the area, ½ × 10 × 24.

questions.s: An equilateral triangle has sides of 6 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: The height is √(6² − 3²) = 3√3, so the area is ½ × 6 × 3√3 = 9√3 cm². The value 18√3 forgets the factor ½.

questions.s: A cylindrical water tank has a diameter of 10 m and a height of 4 m. What is its volume?
questions.e: The radius is 5 m, so the volume is π × 5² × 4 = 100π m³. The value 400π m³ uses the diameter as the radius.

questions.s: A cube-shaped container with inner edges of 10 cm is full of water. All the water is poured into an empty cylinder with an inner base radius of 5 cm, and none spills. How deep is the water in the cylinder?
questions.e: The water's volume is 10³ = 1,000 cm³, and depth = 1,000 ÷ (π × 5²) = 40/π cm. The value 10/π uses the edge 10 as the radius, and 200/π divides by 5π, forgetting to square the radius.

questions.s: Two triangles are similar, and the ratio of their corresponding sides is 2 : 5. The smaller triangle has an area of 12 cm². What is the area of the larger triangle?
questions.e: Areas scale by the square of the side ratio, (5/2)² = 25/4, so the area is 12 × 25/4 = 75 cm². The value 30 cm² scales by 5/2 only.

questions.s: A room floor is a rectangle 6 m long and 4.5 m wide. Tiling costs Rs 800 per square metre. What is the cost of tiling the whole floor?
questions.e: The floor area is 6 × 4.5 = 27 m², and 27 × 800 = Rs 21,600. The value Rs 16,800 uses the perimeter, 21 m, instead of the area.

questions.s: A metal plate is made by cutting a 4 cm by 3 cm rectangle from one corner of a 10 cm by 8 cm rectangle, so that the plate is L-shaped. What is the perimeter of the plate?
questions.e: The two new inner edges (4 cm and 3 cm) exactly replace the 4 cm and 3 cm of outer edge that were removed, so the perimeter stays 2(10 + 8) = 36 cm. The value 29 cm subtracts the removed edges without adding the new ones, and 68 is the area in cm².

questions.s: A closed cylinder has a base radius of 4 cm and a height of 9 cm. What is the area of its curved surface only?
questions.e: The curved surface area is 2πrh = 2 × π × 4 × 9 = 72π cm². The value 104π adds the two circular ends (32π), which the question excludes.

questions.s: A solid cone has a base radius of 5 cm and a slant height of 13 cm. What is its total surface area, including the base?
questions.e: The curved surface is πrl = π × 5 × 13 = 65π and the base is π × 5² = 25π, giving 90π cm². The value 65π leaves out the base, and 85π uses the perpendicular height 12 instead of the slant height.

questions.s: A solid hemisphere has a radius of 3 cm. What is its volume?
questions.e: A hemisphere is half a sphere: ½ × (4/3)π × 3³ = 18π cm³. The value 36π cm³ is the volume of the whole sphere, and 27π is the hemisphere's total surface area, 3πr².

questions.s: A cuboid measures 5 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm. What is its volume?
questions.e: Volume is 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 cm³. The value 94 is the surface area, 2(20 + 15 + 12), in cm².

questions.s: The radius of a cylinder is doubled while its height stays the same. By what factor is its volume multiplied?
questions.e: Volume is πr²h, so doubling r multiplies the volume by 2² = 4. The factor 8 would apply if every length, including the height, were doubled.

questions.s: The radius of a sphere is increased by 50%. By what percent does its volume increase?
questions.e: The new volume is 1.5³ = 3.375 times the old one, an increase of 237.5 %. The value 125 % uses the area factor 1.5² = 2.25, and 337.5 % gives the new volume as a percent of the old rather than the increase.

questions.s: A circle has a circumference of 18π cm. What is its area?
questions.e: From 2πr = 18π, the radius is 9 cm, so the area is π × 9² = 81π cm². The value 324π uses 18 as the radius.

questions.s: A sector of a circle has a radius of 12 cm and an angle of 60° at the centre. What is the area of the sector?
questions.e: The sector is 60/360 = 1/6 of the circle, so its area is 1/6 × 144π = 24π cm². The value 4π is the arc length, 1/6 × 24π.

questions.s: A circular lawn has a radius of 10 m. A path 2 m wide runs all the way round the outside of the lawn. What is the area of the path?
questions.e: The outer radius is 12 m, so the path's area is π(12² − 10²) = 44π m². The value 36π puts the path inside the lawn (10² − 8²), and 40π uses the lawn's circumference times the width.

questions.s: A prism is 10 cm long, and its cross-section is a right-angled triangle whose two shorter sides are 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the volume of the prism?
questions.e: The cross-section has area ½ × 6 × 8 = 24 cm², and 24 × 10 = 240 cm³. The value 480 cm³ forgets the ½, and 400 cm³ wrongly uses the hypotenuse 10 as a perpendicular side.

questions.s: A pyramid has a square base of side 6 cm and a perpendicular height of 10 cm. What is its volume?
questions.e: Volume is ⅓ × base area × height = ⅓ × 36 × 10 = 120 cm³. The value 360 cm³ is the volume of the cuboid with the same base and height, forgetting the ⅓.

questions.s: An empty tank is a cuboid 2 m long, 1.5 m wide and 1.2 m deep. A pump fills it at 120 litres per minute. How long does it take to fill the tank? (1 m³ = 1,000 litres)
questions.e: The volume is 2 × 1.5 × 1.2 = 3.6 m³ = 3,600 litres, and 3,600 ÷ 120 = 30 minutes. The value 3 minutes treats 3.6 m³ as 360 litres instead of 3,600 litres.

questions.s: A solid ball fits exactly inside a cube-shaped box of edge 6 cm, touching all six faces. What is the volume of the space inside the box that is not filled by the ball?
questions.e: The ball's radius is 3 cm, so its volume is (4/3)π × 27 = 36π, leaving 216 − 36π cm³. The value 216 − 12π squares the radius instead of cubing it, and 216 − 9π uses the circle area πr².

questions.s: A triangle has vertices at (0, 0), (8, 0) and (2, 6) in the coordinate plane. What is its area?
questions.e: The base along the x-axis is 8 and the height is the y-coordinate 6, so the area is ½ × 8 × 6 = 24. The value 48 forgets the ½.

questions.s: A regular hexagon has sides of 4 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: A regular hexagon splits into 6 equilateral triangles of side 4, each of area (√3/4) × 16 = 4√3, so the area is 24√3 cm². The value 16√3 uses only 4 triangles, and 48√3 forgets the ½ in each triangle.

questions.s: A room is a cuboid 5 m long, 4 m wide and 3 m high. Its four walls are to be painted, except for a door 1 m wide and 2 m high. What area is to be painted?
questions.e: The four walls have area 2(5 + 4) × 3 = 54 m², and removing the 2 m² door leaves 52 m². The value 54 m² forgets the door, and 72 m² also includes the ceiling.

questions.s: A square has a perimeter of 36 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: Each side is 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm, so the area is 9² = 81 cm². The value 324 cm² squares 18, half the perimeter, as if it were the side.

questions.s: A solid cylinder has a volume of 150 cm³. A cone with the same base and the same height is drilled out of it. What is the volume of the solid that remains?
questions.e: A cone with the same base and height has ⅓ of the cylinder's volume, 50 cm³, so 150 − 50 = 100 cm³ remain. The value 50 cm³ is the volume of the cone that was removed.

questions.s: A rectangle is 9 cm long and 6 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
questions.e: Perimeter is 2(9 + 6) = 30 cm. The value 54 is the area, and 15 cm adds only one length and one width.

questions.s: A circle has a diameter of 10 cm. What is its circumference?
questions.e: Circumference is πd = π × 10 = 10π cm. The value 25π is the area, πr² with r = 5.

questions.s: A triangle has an area of 36 cm² and a base of 9 cm. What is its perpendicular height?
questions.e: From ½ × 9 × h = 36, we get h = 72 ÷ 9 = 8 cm. The value 4 cm divides 36 by 9 and forgets the ½ in the formula.

questions.s: A trapezium has an area of 60 cm² and parallel sides of 7 cm and 13 cm. What is the perpendicular distance between the parallel sides?
questions.e: From ½(7 + 13)h = 60, we get 10h = 60, so h = 6 cm. The value 3 cm divides 60 by 20 and forgets the ½.

questions.s: A cylinder has a base radius of 5 cm and a height of 6 cm. What is its volume?
questions.e: Volume is πr²h = π × 25 × 6 = 150π cm³. The value 60π is the curved surface area 2πrh, and 110π is the total surface area.

questions.s: A cone has a base radius of 3 cm and a slant height of 5 cm. What is its volume?
questions.e: The perpendicular height is √(5² − 3²) = 4 cm, so the volume is ⅓ × π × 9 × 4 = 12π cm³. The value 15π uses the slant height 5 in place of the perpendicular height.

questions.s: A sphere has a radius of 5 cm. What is its surface area?
questions.e: Surface area is 4πr² = 4 × π × 25 = 100π cm². The value 400π uses the diameter 10 in place of the radius.

questions.s: Two boxes are similar, with corresponding lengths in the ratio 3 : 4. The smaller box has a surface area of 90 cm². What is the surface area of the larger box?
questions.e: Areas scale by (4/3)² = 16/9, so the surface area is 90 × 16/9 = 160 cm². The value 120 scales by 4/3 only, and 213⅓ uses the volume factor (4/3)³.

questions.s: Two similar cones have volumes in the ratio 8 : 27. What is the ratio of their curved surface areas?
questions.e: The cube root of 8 : 27 gives the length ratio 2 : 3, and areas scale by its square, 4 : 9. The ratio 2 : 3 is for lengths only, and 16 : 81 is the fourth power of the length ratio.

questions.s: A cube has a volume of 64 cm³. What is its total surface area?
questions.e: An edge is ∛64 = 4 cm, each face is 16 cm², and 6 faces give 96 cm². The value 16 cm² is a single face only.

questions.s: A shape is made of a rectangle 12 cm by 8 cm with a semicircle attached to one of its 8 cm sides, so that the 8 cm side is the semicircle's diameter. What is the area of the shape?
questions.e: The rectangle is 12 × 8 = 96 cm², and the semicircle has radius 4, so its area is ½ × π × 16 = 8π. The value 96 + 16π adds a full circle instead of a half.

questions.s: In a square of side 10 cm, a quarter circle of radius 10 cm is drawn with its centre at one corner of the square, so that its arc joins the two neighbouring corners. What is the area of the part of the square outside the quarter circle?
questions.e: The quarter circle has area ¼ × π × 10² = 25π, so the remaining area is 100 − 25π cm². The value 100 − 5π subtracts the arc length 5π instead of an area.

questions.s: A floor 4.8 m long and 3.6 m wide is to be covered with square tiles of side 60 cm, with no gaps or cutting. How many tiles are needed?
questions.e: Along the length 480 ÷ 60 = 8 tiles fit and along the width 360 ÷ 60 = 6, so 8 × 6 = 48 tiles. The value 28 adds 8 + 6 twice, as if finding a perimeter.

questions.s: A fish tank is a cuboid 50 cm long, 40 cm wide and 30 cm high. How many litres of water does it hold when full? (1 litre = 1,000 cm³)
questions.e: The volume is 50 × 40 × 30 = 60,000 cm³, and 60,000 ÷ 1,000 = 60 litres. The value 600 litres divides by 100 instead of 1,000.

questions.s: A bowl is a hemisphere with an inner radius of 6 cm. How much water can it hold?
questions.e: A hemisphere holds ½ × (4/3)π × 6³ = ½ × 288π = 144π cm³. The value 288π is a full sphere, and 108π is the hemisphere's total surface area 3πr², not a volume.

questions.s: An equilateral triangle has a perimeter of 24 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: Each side is 8 cm, so the area is (√3/4) × 8² = 16√3 cm². The value 32√3 forgets to halve base × height.

questions.s: A square has an area of 49 cm². What is its perimeter?
questions.e: The side is √49 = 7 cm, so the perimeter is 4 × 7 = 28 cm. The value 7 cm is just one side.

questions.s: A solid metal cylinder with a base radius of 3 cm and a height of 16 cm is melted down and recast into solid spheres of radius 3 cm, with no metal wasted. How many spheres are made?
questions.e: The cylinder's volume is π × 9 × 16 = 144π and each sphere's is (4/3)π × 27 = 36π, so 144π ÷ 36π = 4 spheres. The value 12 divides by 12π, which squares the radius instead of cubing it.

questions.s: A closed box is a cuboid measuring 6 cm by 4 cm by 2 cm. What is its total surface area?
questions.e: Surface area is 2(6×4 + 6×2 + 4×2) = 2(24 + 12 + 8) = 88 cm². The value 44 counts each pair of faces only once, and 48 is the volume.

questions.s: The length of a rectangle is increased by 20% and its width is decreased by 10%. By what percent does its area change?
questions.e: The new area is 1.2 × 0.9 = 1.08 times the old one, an increase of 8 %. Simply adding 20 % and −10 % gives 10 %, which ignores that the changes multiply.

questions.s: A sector of a circle has a radius of 9 cm and an angle of 120° at the centre. What is the perimeter of the sector?
questions.e: The arc is 120/360 × 2π × 9 = 6π cm, and the two radii add 18 cm, giving 18 + 6π cm. The value 6π is only the arc, and 9 + 6π counts just one radius.

questions.s: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides of 9 cm and 12 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.e: The hypotenuse is √(81 + 144) = 15 cm, so the perimeter is 9 + 12 + 15 = 36 cm. The value 54 is the area in cm², and 21 cm leaves out the hypotenuse.

questions.s: A pyramid has a square base of side 10 cm. Each of its four triangular faces has a perpendicular height (slant height) of 13 cm. What is the total surface area of the pyramid?
questions.e: The base is 100 cm² and each face is ½ × 10 × 13 = 65 cm², so the total is 100 + 4 × 65 = 360 cm². The value 260 leaves out the base, and 620 forgets the ½ for the triangles.

questions.s: A cone has a volume of 100π cm³ and a base radius of 5 cm. What is its perpendicular height?
questions.e: From ⅓ × π × 25 × h = 100π, we get h = 300 ÷ 25 = 12 cm. The value 4 cm forgets the ⅓, and 60 cm forgets to square the radius.

questions.s: A tank with a rectangular base 40 cm by 25 cm holds some water. A stone of volume 3,000 cm³ is lowered into the tank and is fully covered by the water, which does not overflow. By how much does the water level rise?
questions.e: The rise is the stone's volume divided by the base area: 3,000 ÷ (40 × 25) = 3,000 ÷ 1,000 = 3 cm. The value 7.5 cm divides by 400, which is 40 × 10, not the base area.

questions.s: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One of the two interior angles on the same side of the transversal measures 112°. What is the measure of the other interior angle on that side?
questions.e: Interior angles on the same side of a transversal between parallel lines are supplementary, so the angle is 180° − 112° = 68°. Choosing 112° confuses co-interior angles with alternate angles, which are equal.

questions.s: In triangle PQR, angle P measures 47° and angle Q is twice angle P. What is the measure of angle R?
questions.e: Angle Q = 2 × 47° = 94°, so angle R = 180° − 47° − 94° = 39°. The value 86° comes from subtracting only angle Q from 180°.

questions.s: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 17 cm and one leg of 8 cm. What is the area of the triangle?
questions.e: The other leg is √(17² − 8²) = √225 = 15 cm, so the area is ½ × 8 × 15 = 60 cm². Using the hypotenuse as a base (½ × 8 × 17 = 68) fails because the hypotenuse is not perpendicular to the 8 cm leg.

questions.s: In a 30°-60°-90° triangle, the side opposite the 30° angle is 5 units long. How long is the side opposite the 60° angle?
questions.e: The sides of a 30°-60°-90° triangle are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2, so the side opposite 60° is 5√3. The answer 10 is the hypotenuse, opposite the 90° angle.

questions.s: For an acute angle θ, sin θ = 3/5. What is the value of tan θ?
questions.e: With opposite side 3 and hypotenuse 5, the adjacent side is 4, so tan θ = opposite/adjacent = 3/4. The value 4/3 inverts the ratio, giving adjacent/opposite.

questions.s: What is 210° in radians?
questions.e: Multiply by π/180: 210 × π/180 = 7π/6. The value 7π/3 comes from dividing by 90 instead of 180.

questions.s: Each interior angle of a regular polygon measures 156°. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.e: Each exterior angle is 180° − 156° = 24°, and the exterior angles sum to 360°, so n = 360 ÷ 24 = 15. The answer 24 is the exterior angle itself, not the number of sides.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, point D lies on AB and point E lies on AC so that DE is parallel to BC. If AD = 4, DB = 6 and DE = 6, what is the length of BC?
questions.e: Triangles ADE and ABC are similar with AB = 4 + 6 = 10, so BC = 6 × 10/4 = 15. Using DB instead of AB (6 × 6/4 = 9) compares the wrong pair of lengths.

questions.s: Angle θ lies in the third quadrant and cos θ = −5/13. What is the value of tan θ?
questions.e: In the third quadrant sin θ = −12/13 as well, so tan θ = (−12/13) ÷ (−5/13) = 12/5, positive. Choosing −12/5 forgets that tangent is positive in the third quadrant, where sine and cosine are both negative.

questions.s: An angle is 30° less than twice its complement. What is the measure of the angle?
questions.e: Let the angle be x, so x = 2(90° − x) − 30°, giving 3x = 150° and x = 50°. The value 40° is the complement, not the angle asked for.

questions.s: For 0 < θ < 90°, which expression is equal to (1 − cos²θ)/(sin θ cos θ)?
questions.e: Since 1 − cos²θ = sin²θ, the expression is sin²θ/(sin θ cos θ) = sin θ/cos θ = tan θ. Writing cot θ cancels the wrong factor and leaves cos θ on top.

questions.s: If sin(3x + 10°) = cos(x + 20°) and both angles are acute, what is the value of x?
questions.e: The sine of an acute angle equals the cosine of its complement, so (3x + 10°) + (x + 20°) = 90°, giving 4x = 60° and x = 15°. Setting the two angles equal (x = 5°) treats sine and cosine as the same function.

questions.s: A triangle has sides of 7 cm, 8 cm and 13 cm. What is the measure of its largest angle?
questions.e: By the cosine rule, cos C = (7² + 8² − 13²)/(2 × 7 × 8) = −56/112 = −½, so C = 120°. Getting 60° comes from dropping the minus sign; a negative cosine means the angle is obtuse.

questions.s: An isosceles triangle has two sides of 10 cm and a base of 12 cm. What is its area?
questions.e: The height to the base splits it into halves of 6 cm, so the height is √(10² − 6²) = 8 cm and the area is ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 cm². The value 60 cm² wrongly uses the slanted side of 10 cm as the height.

questions.s: From point A on level ground, the angle of elevation of the top of a minaret is 30°. From point B, 40 m closer to the minaret on the same straight line, the angle of elevation is 60°. What is the height of the minaret?
questions.e: If the height is h, then h√3 − h/√3 = 40, which gives h × 2/√3 = 40 and h = 20√3 m. The answer 40 m is the distance AB, which equals the distance from B to the top, not the height.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, the exterior angle at C measures 125° and angle A measures 50°. What is the measure of angle B?
questions.e: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles, so B = 125° − 50° = 75°. The value 55° is the interior angle at C, not angle B.

questions.s: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 7. What is the measure of the largest angle?
questions.e: The 12 equal parts share 180°, so each part is 15° and the largest angle is 7 × 15° = 105°. The value 126° comes from dividing 180° into 10 parts instead of 12.

questions.s: What is the value of sin(5π/6)?
questions.e: 5π/6 is 150°, in the second quadrant where sine is positive, with reference angle 30°, so sin(5π/6) = sin 30° = 1/2. Choosing −1/2 applies the negative sign that belongs to cosine in this quadrant.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, AB = AC and angle BAC = 36°. The bisector of angle ABC meets side AC at D. What is the measure of angle BDC?
questions.e: Angles B and C are each (180° − 36°)/2 = 72°, so angle DBC = 36° and angle BDC = 180° − 36° − 72° = 72°. The value 108° is angle ADB, the angle on the other side of D.

questions.s: For an acute angle θ, tan θ = 2. What is the value of sin θ cos θ?
questions.e: A right triangle with opposite 2 and adjacent 1 has hypotenuse √5, so sin θ cos θ = (2/√5)(1/√5) = 2/5. The value 4/5 is 2 sin θ cos θ, which is sin 2θ.

questions.s: Two straight lines intersect. One angle formed measures (3x + 15)° and the angle vertically opposite it measures (5x − 25)°. What is the measure of each of these angles?
questions.e: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so 3x + 15 = 5x − 25, giving x = 20 and an angle of 3(20) + 15 = 75°. The value 20° is x itself, and 105° is the adjacent angle.

questions.s: What is the value of sin 30° + cos 60°?
questions.e: sin 30° = 1/2 and cos 60° = 1/2, so the sum is 1. The value (1 + √3)/2 uses cos 30° = √3/2 by mistake.

questions.s: In right triangle ABC, the right angle is at C, AB = 26 and sin A = 5/13. What is the length of BC?
questions.e: BC is opposite angle A, so BC = AB × sin A = 26 × 5/13 = 10. The value 24 is AC, the side adjacent to angle A.

questions.s: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
questions.e: The interior angles of an n-sided polygon sum to (n − 2) × 180°, so a hexagon gives 4 × 180° = 720°. The value 360° is the sum of the exterior angles, which is the same for every polygon.

questions.s: Two triangles are similar, and a pair of corresponding sides measures 3 cm and 5 cm. The area of the smaller triangle is 18 cm². What is the area of the larger triangle?
questions.e: Areas of similar figures scale by the square of the side ratio, so the larger area is 18 × (5/3)² = 18 × 25/9 = 50 cm². The value 30 cm² scales by 5/3 only, as if area grew like length.

questions.s: Which angle is coterminal with −5π/4?
questions.e: Adding one full turn gives −5π/4 + 2π = 3π/4, which ends at the same position. Choosing 5π/4 just drops the minus sign, which reflects the angle instead of turning a full circle.

questions.s: A rectangular field in Multan is 20 m wide and 21 m long. A straight path runs from one corner to the opposite corner. How long is the path?
questions.e: The path is the diagonal, so its length is √(20² + 21²) = √841 = 29 m. The value 41 m adds the two sides, which is the walk around the edge, not the diagonal.

questions.s: For an acute angle θ, sin θ + cos θ = 7/5. What is the value of sin θ cos θ?
questions.e: Squaring gives sin²θ + cos²θ + 2 sin θ cos θ = 49/25, so 2 sin θ cos θ = 49/25 − 1 = 24/25 and sin θ cos θ = 12/25. The value 24/25 forgets to divide by 2.

questions.s: An angle θ in standard position has sin θ < 0 and tan θ > 0. In which quadrant does its terminal side lie?
questions.e: Sine is negative in quadrants III and IV, and tangent is positive in quadrants I and III, so both hold only in quadrant III. Quadrant IV fails because tangent is negative there.

questions.s: Which of the following, given for two triangles, does not on its own guarantee that the triangles are congruent?
o: Two sides and a non-included angle equal
Two sides and the included angle equal
All three pairs of sides equal
Two angles and a corresponding side equal
questions.e: Two sides with an angle that is not between them (SSA) can fit two different triangles, so it does not prove congruence. SAS, SSS and AAS (two angles and a corresponding side) are all valid tests.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, AB = 12, AC = 8 and BC = 15. The bisector of angle A meets BC at D. What is the length of BD?
questions.e: The angle bisector divides BC in the ratio AB : AC = 12 : 8 = 3 : 2, so BD = 15 × 3/5 = 9. The value 6 gives the shorter part, DC, which lies next to the shorter side AC.

questions.s: The diagonal of a square is 8 cm long. What is the area of the square?
questions.e: The side is 8/√2 = 4√2 cm, so the area is (4√2)² = 32 cm²; equivalently, area = diagonal²/2. The value 64 cm² squares the diagonal as if it were a side.

questions.s: Which expression is equal to cos(π − θ) + cos(−θ) for all values of θ?
questions.e: cos(π − θ) = −cos θ and cos(−θ) = cos θ because cosine is even, so the sum is 0. Choosing −2 cos θ wrongly treats cos(−θ) as −cos θ.

questions.s: In right triangle ABC, the right angle is at C. The altitude from C meets hypotenuse AB at D, with AD = 4 and DB = 9. What is the length of CD?
questions.e: Triangles ACD and CBD are similar, so CD² = AD × DB = 36 and CD = 6. The value 36 forgets to take the square root, and 6.5 is half the hypotenuse.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, angle A = 45°, angle B = 60° and BC = 4√2. What is the length of AC?
questions.e: By the sine rule, AC/sin B = BC/sin A, so AC = 4√2 × (√3/2) ÷ (√2/2) = 4√3. The value 8√3/3 comes from swapping sin A and sin B.

questions.s: The vertex angle of an isosceles triangle measures 40°. What is the measure of each base angle?
questions.e: The base angles are equal and share 180° − 40° = 140°, so each is 70°. The value 140° is their total, not each angle.

questions.s: How many values of x with 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π satisfy 2 sin²x = sin x?
questions.e: Factor: sin x (2 sin x − 1) = 0, so sin x = 0 (x = 0, π, 2π) or sin x = 1/2 (x = π/6, 5π/6), giving 5 values. The answer 2 comes from dividing both sides by sin x, which loses the solutions where sin x = 0.

questions.s: Two angles of a triangle measure (2x)° and (3x)°, and the exterior angle at the third vertex measures 110°. What is the measure of the largest interior angle of the triangle?
questions.e: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles, so 5x = 110 and x = 22, giving angles of 44°, 66° and 180° − 110° = 70°. Choosing 66° overlooks the third interior angle, which is the largest.

questions.s: In right triangle XYZ, the right angle is at Y, XY = 7 and YZ = 24. What is the value of cos Z?
questions.e: The hypotenuse is XZ = √(7² + 24²) = 25, and the side adjacent to Z is YZ = 24, so cos Z = 24/25. The value 7/25 is sin Z, using the opposite side.

questions.s: Angle θ lies in the fourth quadrant and cos θ = 1/3. What is the value of sin 2θ?
questions.e: In the fourth quadrant sin θ = −√(1 − 1/9) = −2√2/3, so sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ = 2(−2√2/3)(1/3) = −4√2/9. The value −2√2/9 forgets the factor 2 in the double-angle formula.

questions.s: Three angles lie together on a straight line and measure x°, 2x° and 3x°. What is the measure of the largest of the three angles?
questions.e: Angles on a straight line sum to 180°, so 6x = 180 and x = 30; the largest is 3 × 30° = 90°. The value 30° is x, the smallest angle.

questions.s: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Two corresponding angles measure (4x)° and (x + 54)°. What is the value of x?
questions.e: Corresponding angles are equal, so 4x = x + 54, giving 3x = 54 and x = 18. The value 72 is the angle 4x itself, not x.

questions.s: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 25 cm and one leg of 7 cm. How long is the other leg?
questions.e: The other leg is √(25² − 7²) = √(625 − 49) = √576 = 24 cm. The value 26 cm adds the squares instead of subtracting, which would make the leg longer than the hypotenuse.

questions.s: What is 3π/4 radians in degrees?
questions.e: Multiply by 180/π: 3/4 × 180° = 135°. The value 270° uses 360° in place of 180° for π.

questions.s: What is the value of tan 60° × tan 30°?
questions.e: tan 60° = √3 and tan 30° = 1/√3, so their product is 1. The value 3 squares √3 instead of multiplying by its reciprocal.

questions.s: What is the measure of each exterior angle of a regular octagon?
questions.e: The exterior angles of any polygon sum to 360°, so each exterior angle of a regular octagon is 360° ÷ 8 = 45°. The value 135° is the interior angle.

questions.s: Two sides of a triangle measure 4 cm and 9 cm. Which of the following could be the length of the third side?
questions.e: The third side must be greater than 9 − 4 = 5 and less than 9 + 4 = 13, so only 7 cm works. A side of 5 cm fails because 4 + 5 equals 9, which gives a flat line, not a triangle.

questions.s: The hypotenuse of an isosceles right triangle is 10 cm. How long is each leg?
questions.e: In a 45°-45°-90° triangle the hypotenuse is √2 times a leg, so each leg is 10/√2 = 5√2 cm. The value 10√2 cm multiplies by √2 when it should divide.

questions.s: For an acute angle θ, cos θ = 8/17. What is the value of sin θ?
questions.e: The opposite side is √(17² − 8²) = 15, so sin θ = 15/17. The value 9/17 uses 17 − 8 instead of the Pythagorean theorem.

questions.s: What is the value of tan(7π/6)?
questions.e: 7π/6 is 210°, in the third quadrant where tangent is positive, with reference angle 30°, so tan(7π/6) = tan 30° = √3/3. Choosing −√3/3 forgets that sine and cosine are both negative there, making their ratio positive.

questions.s: A boy 1.5 m tall casts a shadow 2 m long. At the same moment, a flagpole in Islamabad casts a shadow 12 m long. How tall is the flagpole?
questions.e: The sun's rays make similar triangles, so height/shadow is the same: h = 12 × 1.5/2 = 9 m. The value 16 m uses the ratio upside down (12 × 2/1.5).

questions.s: Which expression is equal to (sin θ + cos θ)² − 2 sin θ cos θ for all values of θ?
questions.e: Expanding gives sin²θ + 2 sin θ cos θ + cos²θ − 2 sin θ cos θ = sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. The option 1 − 4 sin θ cos θ comes from subtracting the middle term instead of adding it when expanding.

questions.s: What is the area of an equilateral triangle with sides of 6 cm?
questions.e: The height is 6 × √3/2 = 3√3 cm, so the area is ½ × 6 × 3√3 = 9√3 cm². The value 18√3 cm² forgets the ½ in the area formula.

questions.s: The interior angles of a polygon add up to 1,260°. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.e: Solve (n − 2) × 180 = 1,260: n − 2 = 7, so n = 9. The value 7 is n − 2, the number of triangles the polygon splits into.

questions.s: If sin 40° = cos k° and 0 < k < 90, what is the value of k?
questions.e: The sine of an angle equals the cosine of its complement, so k = 90 − 40 = 50. The value 140 uses the supplement, which relates sines to sines, not sines to cosines.

questions.s: In a right triangle, one acute angle measures 30° and the hypotenuse is 14 cm. How long is the leg adjacent to the 30° angle?
questions.e: The adjacent leg is 14 × cos 30° = 14 × √3/2 = 7√3 cm. The value 7 cm is the leg opposite the 30° angle.

questions.s: An angle of 5π/3 radians is drawn in standard position. In which quadrant does its terminal side lie?
questions.e: 5π/3 is 300°, which lies between 270° and 360°, so the terminal side is in quadrant IV. Quadrant III would need an angle between 180° and 270°.

questions.s: In triangle ABC, AB = 14, AC = 10 and BC = 18. M is the midpoint of AB and N is the midpoint of AC. What is the perimeter of triangle AMN?
questions.e: AM = 7, AN = 5 and the midpoint segment MN is half of BC, so MN = 9 and the perimeter is 7 + 5 + 9 = 21. The value 42 is the perimeter of the whole triangle ABC.

questions.s: A 25 m ladder leans against a vertical wall with its foot 7 m from the wall. The foot then slides 8 m further away from the wall. How far down the wall does the top of the ladder slide?
questions.e: At first the top is √(25² − 7²) = 24 m high; with the foot 15 m away it is √(25² − 15²) = 20 m high, so it slides 4 m. Assuming the top drops as far as the foot moves (8 m) ignores the right-triangle relationship.

questions.s: If sin θ = 0.4, what is the value of sin(π + θ)?
questions.e: Adding π turns the angle half a circle, so sin(π + θ) = −sin θ = −0.4. The value 0.4 treats sine as unchanged, which is true for sin(π − θ), not sin(π + θ).

questions.s: Two sides of a triangle measure 5 cm and 8 cm, and the angle between them is 60°. How long is the third side?
questions.e: By the cosine rule, c² = 5² + 8² − 2 × 5 × 8 × cos 60° = 89 − 40 = 49, so c = 7 cm. The value √129 cm adds the last term instead of subtracting it.

questions.s: Angle θ lies in the second quadrant and tan θ = −3/4. What is the value of sin θ + cos θ?
questions.e: In the second quadrant sin θ = 3/5 and cos θ = −4/5, so their sum is −1/5. The value 1/5 gives the negative sign to sine instead of cosine.

questions.s: In right triangle ABC, the right angle is at C, AC = 6 and BC = 8. Point D lies on AB so that CD is perpendicular to AB. What is the length of AD?
questions.e: AB = 10, and since triangle ACD is similar to triangle ABC, AD = AC²/AB = 36/10 = 3.6. The value 6.4 is DB, and 4.8 is the altitude CD.

questions.s: How many values of θ with 0° ≤ θ < 360° satisfy 2cos²θ − cos θ − 1 = 0?
questions.e: Factor: (2 cos θ + 1)(cos θ − 1) = 0, so cos θ = 1 gives θ = 0° and cos θ = −½ gives θ = 120° and 240°, three values in all. The answer 2 counts only one angle for cos θ = −½ or forgets θ = 0°.

questions.s: In regular pentagon ABCDE, the diagonal AC is drawn. What is the measure of angle BAC?
questions.e: Each interior angle of a regular pentagon is 108°, and triangle ABC is isosceles with AB = BC, so angle BAC = (180° − 108°)/2 = 36°. The value 108° is angle ABC, not angle BAC.

questions.s: A circle has a radius of 9 cm. What is the length of an arc that subtends a central angle of 40°?
questions.e: Arc length = (40/360) × 2π × 9 = (1/9) × 18π = 2π cm. The value 18π cm is the whole circumference, not the 40° part.

questions.s: What is the area of a sector of a circle with radius 6 cm and central angle 120°?
questions.e: Sector area = (120/360) × π × 6² = (1/3) × 36π = 12π cm². The value 4π is the arc length of the sector, not its area.

questions.s: A circle in the xy-plane has the equation (x − 3)² + (y + 2)² = 49. What are its centre and radius?
questions.e: In (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r², the centre is (h, k) = (3, −2) and r² = 49, so r = 7. Reading the centre as (−3, 2) copies the signs inside the brackets instead of reversing them.

questions.s: Points A, B and C lie on a circle with centre O, and C is on the major arc AB. If angle AOB = 110°, what is the measure of angle ACB?
questions.e: An inscribed angle is half the central angle on the same arc, so angle ACB = 110° ÷ 2 = 55°. The value 125° would be the inscribed angle from a point on the minor arc, which stands on the other 250° arc.

questions.s: AB is a diameter of a circle and C is another point on the circle. If angle CAB = 34°, what is the measure of angle ABC?
questions.e: An angle in a semicircle is a right angle, so angle ACB = 90° and angle ABC = 180° − 90° − 34° = 56°. The value 146° subtracts only the 34° from 180°, forgetting the right angle at C.

questions.s: An arc of length 15 cm lies on a circle of radius 6 cm. What is the central angle of the arc in radians?
questions.e: In radians, angle = arc length ÷ radius = 15 ÷ 6 = 2.5. The value 0.4 divides the radius by the arc length, the wrong way round.

questions.s: Point P is 13 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm. A tangent from P touches the circle at T. What is the length of PT?
questions.e: The radius to T is perpendicular to the tangent, so triangle OTP is right-angled at T and PT = √(13² − 5²) = 12 cm. The value 8 cm subtracts the lengths instead of their squares.

questions.s: What is the radius of the circle x² + y² − 6x + 8y = 0?
questions.e: Completing the square gives (x − 3)² + (y + 4)² = 9 + 16 = 25, so the radius is 5. The value 25 is r², not r.

questions.s: A circle has centre (1, 2) and passes through the point (4, 6). Which is an equation of the circle?
questions.e: The radius is the distance from (1, 2) to (4, 6), √(3² + 4²) = 5, so the right side is r² = 25. Writing 5 on the right confuses r with r².

questions.s: Quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in a circle. Angle A measures (3x)° and angle C measures (x + 20)°. What is the measure of angle A?
questions.e: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary, so 4x + 20 = 180, x = 40 and angle A = 120°. The value 40° is x, and 60° is angle C.

questions.s: A sector is cut from a circle of radius 10 cm with a central angle of 72°. What is the perimeter of the sector?
questions.e: The arc is (72/360) × 2π × 10 = 4π cm, and the perimeter adds the two radii: 20 + 4π cm. The value 4π cm is the arc alone, and 10 + 4π counts only one radius.

questions.s: A chord 16 cm long is drawn in a circle of radius 10 cm. What is the distance from the centre of the circle to the chord?
questions.e: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, giving a right triangle with hypotenuse 10 and leg 8, so the distance is √(100 − 64) = 6 cm. The value 8 cm is half the chord, not the distance.

questions.s: From an external point P, two tangents touch a circle with centre O at points A and B. If angle APB = 50°, what is the measure of angle AOB?
questions.e: In quadrilateral OAPB the angles at A and B are 90°, so angle AOB = 360° − 90° − 90° − 50° = 130°. The value 100° doubles 50° as if P were on the circle, which applies to inscribed angles only.

questions.s: A sector of a circle of radius 9 cm has an arc length of 6π cm. What is the area of the sector?
questions.e: Sector area = ½ × radius × arc length = ½ × 9 × 6π = 27π cm². The value 54π leaves out the ½, and 81π is the area of the whole circle.

questions.s: A circle of radius 4 has its centre in the second quadrant and is tangent to both the x-axis and the y-axis. Which is an equation of the circle?
questions.e: Tangent to both axes means the centre is 4 units from each, and in the second quadrant that is (−4, 4), giving (x + 4)² + (y − 4)² = 16. The equation with (x − 4) and (y + 4) has its centre at (4, −4), in the fourth quadrant.

questions.s: The point (k, 3) lies on the circle x² + y² − 4x = 21, and k is positive. What is the value of k?
questions.e: Substituting y = 3 gives k² − 4k + 9 = 21, so k² − 4k − 12 = 0 = (k − 6)(k + 2) and the positive root is k = 6. The value 2 is the x-coordinate of the centre, not a point on the circle.

questions.s: The line y = x + c is tangent to the circle x² + y² = 8, and c > 0. What is the value of c?
questions.e: Substituting gives 2x² + 2cx + c² − 8 = 0, which has one solution when the discriminant 4c² − 8(c² − 8) = 0, so c² = 16 and c = 4. The value 2√2 is the radius, but the line's y-intercept is farther out than that because the line is slanted.

questions.s: A square is inscribed in a circle of radius 6 cm, with all four of its vertices on the circle. What is the area of the region inside the circle but outside the square?
questions.e: The square's diagonal is the diameter, 12 cm, so its area is 12²/2 = 72 cm² and the region is 36π − 72 cm². Using 144 treats the diameter as the side of the square, which would not fit inside the circle.

questions.s: The minute hand of a clock is 12 cm long. How far does its tip travel in 20 minutes?
questions.e: In 20 minutes the hand turns one third of a circle, so the tip travels (1/3) × 2π × 12 = 8π cm. The value 4π cm uses the formula with the radius but forgets the factor 2 in 2πr.

questions.s: The circles x² + y² = 25 and (x − 6)² + y² = r² touch each other externally, and r > 0. What is the value of r?
questions.e: The centres (0, 0) and (6, 0) are 6 apart, and for external tangency the distance equals the sum of the radii, so 5 + r = 6 and r = 1. The value 11 gives internal tangency, where the distance is the difference of the radii.

questions.s: A circle has an area of 49π cm². What is its circumference?
questions.e: From πr² = 49π, r = 7 cm, so the circumference is 2π × 7 = 14π cm. The value 7π cm uses πr, forgetting the factor 2.

questions.s: A tangent from point P touches a circle with centre O at point T. If angle OPT = 28°, what is the measure of angle TOP?
questions.e: The radius OT is perpendicular to the tangent, so angle OTP = 90° and angle TOP = 180° − 90° − 28° = 62°. The value 152° forgets the right angle at T.

questions.s: The endpoints of a diameter of a circle are (−2, 5) and (6, −1). What are the coordinates of the centre?
questions.e: The centre is the midpoint of the diameter: ((−2 + 6)/2, (5 + (−1))/2) = (2, 2). The point (4, −3) takes half the differences of the coordinates instead of half the sums.

questions.s: Points A, B, C and D lie on a circle, with C and D on the same arc cut off by chord AB. If angle ACB = 47°, what is the measure of angle ADB?
questions.e: Inscribed angles standing on the same arc are equal, so angle ADB = 47°. The value 94° is the central angle on arc AB, not another inscribed angle.

questions.s: In a circle of radius 12 cm, a central angle measures π/3 radians. What is the length of the arc it subtends?
questions.e: With the angle in radians, arc length = radius × angle = 12 × π/3 = 4π cm. The value 36π comes from dividing 12 by 1/3 instead of multiplying.

questions.s: A circle has its centre at the origin and passes through the point (5, −12). Which is an equation of the circle?
questions.e: The radius is √(5² + 12²) = 13, so the equation is x² + y² = 13² = 169. Writing 13 on the right uses r where the equation needs r².

questions.s: What is the radius of the circle 2x² + 2y² − 8x + 12y − 6 = 0?
questions.e: Divide by 2 to get x² + y² − 4x + 6y − 3 = 0, then complete the square: (x − 2)² + (y + 3)² = 4 + 9 + 3 = 16, so r = 4. The value √10 subtracts the 3 instead of moving it to the right-hand side.

questions.s: Which point lies inside the circle (x − 2)² + (y + 1)² = 20?
questions.e: For (5, 2): 3² + 3² = 18, which is less than 20, so the point is inside. The point (6, 1) gives 4² + 2² = 20 exactly, so it lies on the circle, not inside it.

questions.s: An arc of a circle of radius 9 cm has a length of 3π cm. What is the central angle of the arc in degrees?
questions.e: The angle in radians is 3π ÷ 9 = π/3, which is 60°. The value 120° compares the arc with πr instead of 2πr.

questions.s: What is the area of a sector with radius 8 cm and central angle 3π/4 radians?
questions.e: With the angle in radians, sector area = ½r²θ = ½ × 64 × 3π/4 = 24π cm². The value 48π leaves out the ½, and 6π is the arc length.

questions.s: AB is a chord of a circle with centre O, and angle OAB = 25°. Point C lies on the major arc AB. What is the measure of angle ACB?
questions.e: Triangle OAB is isosceles (OA = OB), so angle AOB = 180° − 2 × 25° = 130°, and the inscribed angle ACB is half of that, 65°. The value 130° is the central angle itself.

questions.s: A tangent to a circle touches it at point A. Chord AB makes an angle of 70° with the tangent, and point C lies on the arc of the circle on the other side of AB from that 70° angle. What is the measure of angle ACB?
questions.e: By the alternate segment theorem, the angle between a tangent and a chord equals the inscribed angle on the chord in the opposite segment, so angle ACB = 70°. The value 140° is the central angle on chord AB.

questions.s: The circle x² + y² = 9 is moved 2 units to the right and 5 units down. Which is an equation of the new circle?
questions.e: The new centre is (2, −5) and the radius stays 3, giving (x − 2)² + (y + 5)² = 9. The version with (x + 2) and (y − 5) moves the circle left and up instead.

questions.s: Chords AB and CD of a circle intersect at point E. AE = 4, EB = 9, and E is the midpoint of CD. What is the length of CD?
questions.e: By the intersecting chords theorem, CE × ED = AE × EB = 36, and CE = ED, so each is 6 and CD = 12. The value 6 is only half of CD.

questions.s: The radii of two circles are in the ratio 2 : 5. The circumference of the larger circle is 30π cm. What is the area of the smaller circle?
questions.e: The larger radius is 30π ÷ 2π = 15 cm, so the smaller radius is 15 × 2/5 = 6 cm and its area is 36π cm². The value 12π is the smaller circumference, and 225π is the larger area.

questions.s: A wheel of radius 0.5 m rolls without slipping along a straight road for 100π m. How many complete turns does it make?
questions.e: One turn covers the circumference, 2π × 0.5 = π m, so 100π m takes 100π ÷ π = 100 turns. The value 200 uses πr = 0.5π m as the distance per turn.

questions.s: A circle has its centre on the x-axis and passes through the points (0, 4) and (6, 2). What is its radius?
questions.e: With centre (h, 0), equal distances give h² + 16 = (6 − h)² + 4, so 12h = 24 and h = 2; the radius is √(2² + 4²) = 2√5. The value 2 is h, the x-coordinate of the centre.

questions.s: Chord PQ of a circle with centre O and radius 6 cm subtends a right angle at O. What is the area of the smaller region between chord PQ and arc PQ?
questions.e: The quarter-circle sector OPQ has area ¼ × 36π = 9π, and triangle OPQ has area ½ × 6 × 6 = 18, so the segment is 9π − 18 cm². The value 9π − 36 forgets the ½ in the triangle's area.

questions.s: From point P, two tangents are drawn to a circle of radius 6 cm, touching it at A and B. If angle APB = 60°, how long is each tangent PA?
questions.e: OP bisects angle APB, so in right triangle OAP the angle at P is 30° and PA = OA ÷ tan 30° = 6√3 cm. The value 12 cm is OP, the distance from P to the centre.

questions.s: The line y = 3 crosses the circle x² + y² − 2x − 24 = 0 at two points. What is the distance between these points?
questions.e: Substituting y = 3 gives x² − 2x − 15 = 0, so x = 5 or x = −3 and the points are 8 apart. The value 10 is the diameter, which the line would cut only if it passed through the centre (1, 0).

questions.s: A circular pond has a diameter of 18 m. What is its circumference?
questions.e: Circumference = π × diameter = 18π m. The value 36π m doubles the diameter, treating it as the radius in 2πr.

questions.s: What is the area of a circle with a diameter of 10 cm?
questions.e: The radius is 5 cm, so the area is π × 5² = 25π cm². The value 100π squares the diameter instead of the radius.

questions.s: What are the centre and radius of the circle x² + (y − 5)² = 36?
questions.e: Written as (x − 0)² + (y − 5)² = 6², the centre is (0, 5) and the radius is 6. Centre (0, −5) copies the minus sign instead of reversing it.

questions.s: An inscribed angle of a circle measures 35°. What is the measure of the central angle that stands on the same arc?
questions.e: A central angle is twice any inscribed angle on the same arc, so it measures 2 × 35° = 70°. The value 17.5° halves instead of doubling.

questions.s: What is the area of a sector of a circle with radius 4 cm and central angle 90°?
questions.e: A 90° sector is a quarter of the circle, so its area is ¼ × π × 4² = 4π cm². The value 2π is the arc length of the quarter circle.

questions.s: OA and OB are radii of a circle with centre O, and angle AOB = 100°. What is the measure of angle OAB?
questions.e: Triangle OAB is isosceles because OA = OB, so angles OAB and OBA are each (180° − 100°)/2 = 40°. The value 50° halves 100° instead of halving what remains of 180°.

questions.s: A right triangle with legs of 6 cm and 8 cm has all three vertices on a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.e: A right angle inscribed in a circle stands on a diameter, so the hypotenuse √(6² + 8²) = 10 cm is the diameter and the radius is 5 cm. The value 10 cm is the diameter.

questions.s: What is the centre of the circle x² + y² + 10x − 4y + 4 = 0?
questions.e: Completing the square gives (x + 5)² + (y − 2)² = 25, so the centre is (−5, 2). The point (5, −2) keeps the signs of the coefficients instead of reversing them, and (−10, 4) forgets to halve them.

questions.s: A circle has a radius of 15 cm. What is the length of an arc that subtends a central angle of 2π/5 radians?
questions.e: With the angle in radians, arc length = rθ = 15 × 2π/5 = 6π cm. The value 3π cm drops the factor 2 in the angle, and 30π cm is the whole circumference.

questions.s: A sector of a circle of radius 6 cm has an area of 15π cm². What is its central angle?
questions.e: The whole circle has area 36π, so the sector is 15/36 = 5/12 of it, and 5/12 × 360° = 150°. The value 75° halves the correct fraction, as if the circle's area were 72π.

questions.s: Quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in a circle, and angle ABC = 95°. What is the measure of angle ADC?
questions.e: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°, so angle ADC = 180° − 95° = 85°. The value 95° assumes opposite angles are equal, which holds for a parallelogram, not a general cyclic quadrilateral.

questions.s: From an external point P, tangents PA and PB touch a circle at A and B. If angle PAB = 65°, what is the measure of angle APB?
questions.e: Tangents from one point are equal, so triangle PAB is isosceles with angles PAB = PBA = 65°, leaving angle APB = 180° − 130° = 50°. The value 115° subtracts only one base angle.

questions.s: In a circle of radius 13 cm, a chord lies 5 cm from the centre. How long is the chord?
questions.e: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so half the chord is √(13² − 5²) = 12 cm and the chord is 24 cm. The value 12 cm forgets to double the half-chord.

questions.s: A circle has centre (3, −5) and is tangent to the x-axis. Which is an equation of the circle?
questions.e: The distance from the centre to the x-axis is |−5| = 5, so r = 5 and r² = 25. The version ending in 9 uses the distance to the y-axis, which would make the circle tangent to the y-axis instead.

questions.s: The points (1, 1) and (7, 9) are the endpoints of a diameter of a circle. Which is an equation of the circle?
questions.e: The centre is the midpoint (4, 5), and the radius is half of √(6² + 8²) = 10, so r² = 25. The version ending in 100 uses the diameter as the radius.

questions.s: Two circles share the same centre and have radii of 5 cm and 7 cm. What is the area of the ring between them?
questions.e: The ring's area is π × 7² − π × 5² = 49π − 25π = 24π cm². The value 4π squares the difference of the radii, (7 − 5)², instead of subtracting the squares.

questions.s: AB is a diameter of a circle of length 10 cm, and C is a point on the circle with AC = 6 cm. What is the length of BC?
questions.e: Angle ACB is 90° because it stands on a diameter, so BC = √(10² − 6²) = 8 cm. The value 2√34 cm adds the squares, treating AB as a leg instead of the hypotenuse.

questions.s: A pendulum 30 cm long swings through an angle of 0.4 radians. What is the length of the arc traced by its tip?
questions.e: With the angle in radians, arc length = rθ = 30 × 0.4 = 12 cm, and no π is needed. The value 12π cm treats 0.4 as if it were a multiple of π.

questions.s: The circle (x − 1)² + (y − k)² = 25 passes through the point (4, 0), and k > 0. What is the value of k?
questions.e: Substituting gives 3² + k² = 25, so k² = 16 and k = 4. The value 16 is k², not k.

questions.s: Points A, B and C lie on a circle with centre O, and B is on the major arc AC. If angle ABC = 40°, what is the measure of angle OAC?
questions.e: The central angle AOC is 2 × 40° = 80°, and triangle OAC is isosceles, so angle OAC = (180° − 80°)/2 = 50°. The value 80° is angle AOC itself.

questions.s: The circle x² + y² + 6x − 2y = k has a radius of 5. What is the value of k?
questions.e: Completing the square gives (x + 3)² + (y − 1)² = k + 9 + 1, so k + 10 = 25 and k = 15. The value 35 subtracts 9 and 1 instead of adding them to the right-hand side.

questions.s: An equilateral triangle is inscribed in a circle of radius 4 cm. What is the side length of the triangle?
questions.e: Each side subtends a central angle of 120°, so by the cosine rule s² = 4² + 4² − 2 × 4 × 4 × cos 120° = 48 and s = 4√3 cm. The value 8 cm is the diameter, which is longer than any side of the triangle.

questions.s: Which is an equation of the line tangent to the circle x² + y² = 25 at the point (3, 4)?
questions.e: The radius to (3, 4) has slope 4/3, so the tangent has slope −3/4 and passes through (3, 4), giving 3x + 4y = 25. The line 4x − 3y = 0 is the radius line itself, not the tangent.

questions.s: In a circle of radius 10 cm, chord AB is also 10 cm long. What is the length of the minor arc AB?
questions.e: Triangle OAB has three sides of 10 cm, so it is equilateral and angle AOB = 60°; the arc is (60/360) × 20π = 10π/3 cm. The value 20π/3 cm corresponds to 120°.

questions.s: What is the distance between the centres of the circles x² + y² − 4x = 0 and x² + y² + 6y = 0?
questions.e: The centres are (2, 0) and (0, −3), found by completing the square, so the distance is √(2² + 3²) = √13. The value 5 is the sum of the radii, 2 + 3, not the distance between the centres.
